problem.text: Find the probability that a randomly selected divisor of $20!$ is a multiple of $2000$.

steps.title: Where to start: prime factorize both numbers
steps.body: A divisor of $20!$ is built by choosing an exponent for each prime of $20!$, from $0$ up to the exponent in $20!$. Being a multiple of $2000$ is also a condition on exponents. So we need the prime factorizations of $2000$ and $20!$.

steps.title: Only the primes 2 and 5 matter
steps.body: Legendre's formula finds the exponent of a prime $p$ in $20!$: add $\lfloor 20/p \rfloor + \lfloor 20/p^2 \rfloor + \dots$. We only need $p = 2$ and $p = 5$, because the other primes in a divisor are free and do not affect whether it is a multiple of $2000$.

your_turn.prompt: Find the exponents of $2$ and $5$ in $20!$.

steps.title: Count exponent choices
steps.body: A random divisor picks its exponent of $2$ from $0$ to $18$ and its exponent of $5$ from $0$ to $4$, each value equally often, and these choices are independent. It is a multiple of $2000$ when the exponent of $2$ is at least $4$ and the exponent of $5$ is at least $3$. Careful: $0$ is an allowed exponent, so $0$ to $18$ is $19$ choices, not $18$.

your_turn.prompt: How many allowed exponents of $2$ are at least $4$, out of how many? Same question for $5$ and at least $3$.
your_turn.answer: For $2$: $4$ through $18$ is $15$ out of $19$. For $5$: $3$ or $4$ is $2$ out of $5$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
The exponents of the other primes cancel out, since they are free in both the good divisors and all divisors. Multiply the two independent chances.
$$\frac{15}{19}\cdot\frac{2}{5} = \frac{30}{95} = \frac{6}{19}$$
The answer is **$\frac{6}{19}$**.
